item.title: Ciencia para futuros tomadores de decisión
item.description: Energy, warming, health, logistics, quantum computing: the political and economic questions increasingly turn on technical content, and a leader who misreads the science will decide badly. The concepts and techniques that help someone decide, for people who already make decisions and people who are about to.

item.title: ¿Quién escribe la función objetivo?
item.description: Who decides what an artificial intelligence should optimise? Advanced manufacturing is the case: the question is not what the technology can do but how the objective function gets written, and by whom — which is the decision that gets automated along with everything else.

item.title: triage-pg
item.description: Temporal machine learning for public policy, end to end inside PostgreSQL. A fork of the University of Chicago’s Triage in which cohorts, labels, features, temporal cross-validation and model governance are all expressed as SQL against the database that already holds the data, so a pipeline moves to production without leaving it.

item.title: featurizer
item.description: Deep Feature Synthesis compiled to SQL. Given a relational schema and an entity graph, it generates the point-in-time-correct feature matrix as queries the database runs itself, so the database computes each feature as of a date rather than joining it after the fact.

item.title: Ciencia de Datos para Políticas Públicas
item.description: Turning analysis into action, and deliberately not a course on machine-learning methods. Built on Rayid Ghani and Kit Rodolfa’s Machine Learning in Practice at Carnegie Mellon, which itself comes out of the Data Science for Social Good fellowship.

item.title: Positioning Medicine Across a National Hospital Network
item.description:
A public health system of national coverage — unnamed by agreement — runs sixty-four warehouses that supply 1,456 medical units. Critical medicines stocked out while others expired on the shelf: the network held inventory, but in the wrong places, and first-expired-first-out losses compounded the misallocation.

Inventory positioned by local judgment, shelf by shelf, across a network too large for judgment: shortages of critical medicines in some units coexisted with expiry losses in others.

item.title: State-Guided Optimization: The Chinese Approach
item.description: Operations research for national infrastructure networks, taught through the way one state directs them. Twelve weeks organised around the claim that an objective function is a political statement about who is served first — the same argument the rest of this site makes, worked out at the length a course allows.

item.title: Machine Learning as Performative Materialist Practice: Thirteen Theses on the Epistemology, Methodology, and Politics of Applied ML
item.description: Thirteen numbered theses on what the field optimizes, for whom, and what it refuses to count. Under review; the preprint stays citable throughout.

item.title: Fewer Unproductive Moves at a Container Terminal
item.description:
Most yard moves at a container terminal earn nothing: containers are dug out, re-stacked, and shuffled aside to reach others. At the terminal in the study, three of every four movements were unproductive, and about half of those traced to pre-clearance service requests — the administrative previo a customs broker asks for, distinct from formal customs inspection — that arrive with little warning (Villalobos et al. 2026).

The terminal's operating rules flagged which containers would request pre-clearance service with 25 % precision and 30 % recall — most service requests arrived as surprises, and every surprise meant digging a container out of a stack built without it in mind.

item.title: Toward Reducing Unproductive Container Moves: Predicting Service Requirements and Dwell Times
item.description: Two models over a container terminal’s operational data: which containers will request pre-clearance service, and how long each will dwell in the yard. Evaluated with temporal validation against the terminal’s operating rules; the paper estimates a reduction of 13 % to 23 % of total handling operations (Villalobos et al. 2026).

item.title: Cuando el Software se Disuelve
item.description: A live demo takes one prompt from raw data to a finished dashboard, and the talk asks what it means that the product dissolved into the prompt. It closes on a sustained critique of Acemoglu’s Simple Macroeconomics of AI: the modest 1.2% follows from the shape of the model — Hulten’s theorem and an exogenous task taxonomy — and restoring the feedback loop he excludes overturns the conclusion. Choosing the formal framework is itself a political choice about what the model is permitted to find.

item.title: Advanced Claude Code Workflows
item.description: Seven primitives — CLAUDE.md, hooks, skills, subagents, teams, commands and session management — argued as the unit of reuse in a data-science practice, in place of prompts. Context rot is the constraint the whole design answers to, and the talk ends on a minimal setup and a maturity ladder to start from on Monday.

item.title: Designing AI for Prosecutorial Governance: Case Prioritization and Statutory Oversight in Mexico
Primetime Satan: Fear-Based Media Exposure, Moral Panic, and Electoral Behavior
Simulating Reality: From AlphaGo to AlphaEvolve
item.description: The thesis comes first: encode the norm — objectives and limits — as an executable harness, and evolutionary search over code can explore the policies and heuristics that maximise welfare under verifiable constraints. Built from Move 37 through AlphaFold to AlphaEvolve and tested against Hassabis’s conjecture that any pattern in nature can be modelled efficiently by classical algorithms, it closes on what that makes programmable, auditable and measurable in public policy, with the Corredor Interoceánico as the worked case.

item.title: Systems concepts for public policy
item.description: Systems thinking, complex adaptive systems and systems engineering put to societal problems — past the linear and reductionist habit, toward interdisciplinary and systemic policy.

item.title: Some examples to get the conversation going
Los LLM como preservadores de variedad
item.description: Read through Lyapunov stability, Prigogine’s dissipative structures and Beer’s Viable System Model: a trained model reduces variety in Ashby’s sense while a language model preserves it, and that difference decides where each one belongs.

item.title: Los nuevos retos del CIO ante la IA
Taller de Inteligencia Artificial
item.description: A survey for faculty across the whole stack — supervised learning, reinforcement learning, deep learning and generative models — organised around what each one makes possible rather than how it works, and worked through a live unemployment-prediction example with applications in health, environment and education.

item.title: IA y Toma de Decisiones
item.description: Machine learning, reinforcement learning and generative models set against the decisions they can actually change, with centaurs — human-and-model pairings — as the working unit. The hard part is not the model but naming the decision and the action it enables.

item.title: Cognitive modeling for understanding interactions between people and decision support tools in complex and uncertain environments: A study protocol
Descifrando la próxima década de las telecomunicaciones y la economía digital
Current research trends on cognition, integrative complexity, and decision-making: a systematic literature review using activity theory and neuroscience
Inspecciones
item.description: The state must verify that people and firms comply with far more rules than it can ever inspect, so the real question is which inspections to run. A course on prioritising scarce enforcement capacity.
